scoring_justification: We recompute the wetting/non‑wetting classification from the raw coverage‑vs‑pressure table and recompute the H₂ jump interval and monotonicity from the raw μ*‑coverage table. No need for hidden labels; all gold references are paper‑reported qualitative/quantitative descriptions.

hidden_assets.purpose: Expected wetting/non‑wetting for each (T, D) condition for Ne; μ* jump intervals for H₂ at 18 K and 22 K; continuous‑growth requirement at 30 K.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: Fig. 1+2+3 and explicit sentences ("… jump between μ*=−2.68 and −2.65 at 18 K … between −2.68 and −2.678 at 22 K … continuous growth at 30 K"); Ne: Fig. 1/2 descriptions (wetting for D=75 K at 34.3 K, nonwetting for D=50 K at 34.3 K, wetting for D=50 K at 40.7 K, nonwetting for D=14 K at 40.7 K).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Direct literal extraction from the paper; tolerances ±0.02 chosen to absorb typical Monte‑Carlo run‑to‑run spread while excluding guesses outside the described transition region.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own reported values, verified against the source text and figure captions.

outputs.description: Ne adsorption isotherms; the checker classifies wetting/non‑wetting from coverage at the highest pressure for each condition, without requiring absolute units.
H₂ adsorption isotherms; the checker identifies the μ* interval of the abrupt coverage jump (incomplete wetting) and verifies continuous monotonic growth at 30 K (complete wetting).

output_contract.notes: The checker uses structural audit and threshold logic: for hydrogen, it locates the μ* range where coverage jumps by >80% and checks it falls within paper‑reported intervals; for neon, it classifies wetting by whether the coverage at the highest pressure exceeds or stays below hidden fractional thresholds. All values of potential parameters and conditions needed for simulation are provided in the action descriptions.
